Well, no, you know, first of all, you know, whether it's the oil industry or agriculture or the restaurant industry, we have to get America going. And people talk about what is going to happen in phase four. And I'm telling you what phase four is, is figuring out a safe, responsible way to open up business. Japan, South Korea are our top importers of beef. We need them to get rolling again. We need China to come back online. The President's worked on some incredible trade agreements that I was very proud to be part of. And we haven't been able to really implement those. The tariffs are coming down. They're equal now. So we've got great opportunities there. We need restaurants to be able to open. I don't tell you this or your listeners that the high end stakes don't have a destination right now. The other thing I try to communicate to the White House, and I think successfully is that agriculture was the first one impacted by the virus. Way back in January, a month before the airlines were screaming, agriculture had the bottom fall out of already troubling markets. We lost another 25%. And I think that was basically due to Japan and Korea and China shutting down all the imports as well. So part of the response is $19 billion for agriculture. So $19 billion with a B, And a large portion that probably I'm going to guess around 5% is going to be for the livestock industry. So we've been working with Secretary Perdue to see what as he gets ready to roll that out. And I'm expecting end to have announcements this week, what that's going to look like for next week. I just think most people understand the cash it takes to leverage a feedlot operation in today's world. And so we're trying to revisit that as well.
